title: Asynchronous IoT Sensor Aggregator
business: Industrial manufacturing firms managing thousands of remote sensors.
problem: High-latency data ingestion bottlenecks caused by synchronous processing of incoming sensor telemetry streams.
solution: Utilizing Go's built-in concurrency primitives, specifically goroutines and channels, to decouple network ingestion from data processing, allowing the system to handle thousands of concurrent connections without blocking.
steps: Define a struct to represent the incoming sensor telemetry data packet.
Implement a listener using net/http to accept incoming sensor requests.
Spawn a goroutine for each incoming request to handle processing asynchronously.
Use channels to safely pass processed data to a background storage worker.
Compile the application into a single static binary for deployment to lightweight container environments.
outcome: Improved system responsiveness and the ability to scale ingestion capacity linearly with available CPU resources.
limitation: Goroutines are lightweight but not infinite; excessive spawning without a worker pool can lead to memory exhaustion, which is monitored by checking the runtime memory statistics.
